# Data Model: Feature-Vector Grounding (Epic 040)

**Generated by**: `/speckit-plan` | **Date**: 2026-06-26

This document captures the complete shape of every new or changed field introduced by this epic.
It is the authoritative reference for both implementation and glossary authoring. No field may
be shipped without a matching entry in `docs/architecture/feature-vector-glossary.md`.

---

## 1. `runSparseLookahead` return shape (sparseLookahead.js)

All new fields are added to the existing return object. The existing fields
(`case`, `tag`, `aliasMap`, `allowedSetEntries`, `oppTag`, etc.) are unchanged.

### 1.1 `outcomeTiming` (Story A — new field)

```js
outcomeTiming: {
  best:   { outcome: 'win' | 'draw' | 'loss', pliesToEnd: number | null },
  played: { outcome: 'win' | 'draw' | 'loss', pliesToEnd: number | null },
}
```

- `outcome` = `outcomeWithBestPlay(score)` — same derivation as the existing `bestOutcome` /
  `postBlunderOutcome` fields; `"win"` | `"draw"` | `"loss"` (not the `_with_best_play` suffix
  used in the feature vector's `bestOutcome` field — see projection §3.1 for the mapping).
  Wait — actually let me align with the existing `bestOutcome` naming. Looking at the spec again:
  `outcomeTiming.best.outcome ∈ win|draw|loss` (shorter, for the timing sub-object), while the
  top-level `lookahead.bestOutcome` keeps `win_with_best_play` | `draw_with_best_play` |
  `loss_with_best_play`. These are two separate fields — `outcomeTiming` uses the short form.
- `pliesToEnd` = `Math.abs(score)` when `score !== 0 && score !== undefined`; `null` otherwise.
  Derived free from the pre-move `solver.query(movestring)` results already in scope.
- Distinct from `realizedOnPly` (mistake-branch depth) — see glossary §5.3.

**Presence rule**: `outcomeTiming` MUST be present on every one of the four return paths of
`runSparseLookahead` — it is NOT conditional on reachability or any other field. It is legitimately
absent ONLY when the `lookahead` block itself is absent (lookahead did not run at all). Within a
returned lookahead, `outcomeTiming` is always spread in; a `null` pliesToEnd (draw or solver error)
does NOT justify omitting the field — the `outcome` sub-field still carries information. A
positional/no-forced-outcome position produces `outcome: 'draw'` with `pliesToEnd: null` (not
absent). `outcomeTiming` is NEVER pruned by `pruneEmpty` (it is always non-empty due to the
`outcome` field being a non-empty string).

**Derivation** (inside `runSparseLookahead`, after the pre-move query):
```js
const toOutcome = (score) =>
  score === undefined ? null
  : score > 0 ? 'win'
  : score === 0 ? 'draw'
  : 'loss';

const toPliesToEnd = (score) =>
  score === undefined || score === 0 ? null : Math.abs(score);

const outcomeTiming = {
  best:   { outcome: toOutcome(optScore),     pliesToEnd: toPliesToEnd(optScore)     },
  played: { outcome: toOutcome(blunderScore), pliesToEnd: toPliesToEnd(blunderScore) },
};
```

### 1.2 `decisiveLine` (Story A — new field)

```js
decisiveLine: {
  owner:                  'player' | 'opponent',
  cells:                  string[],   // 4-cell window, cNrM (1-indexed, as in all glossary cells)
  completingCell:         string,     // the unique gravity-top cell in the window
  winningLinesThroughCell: number,   // 1 = single-line win; >1 = genuine fork
  fastSide:              'best' | 'played',  // which move line surfaces this win soonest
  fastSideRealizedOnPly:  number,    // ply at which the fastest side's immediate_threat fires
  slowSideRealizedOnPly:  number | null, // ply for the other side; null = not found within horizon
} | null  // null (absent after pruning) when no immediate_threat within search horizon
```

**Derivation** (per-path helper invoked at EACH of the four return paths):
```js
// Find earliest immediate_threat way from a tally
function pickEarliestWay(tally) {
  const entry = tally.get('immediate_threat');
  if (!entry || entry.ways.length === 0) return null;
  return entry.ways.reduce((best, w) => (!best || w.ply < best.ply) ? w : best, null);
}

// Assemble decisiveLine from the correct source tally and explicit owner.
// Called at EACH return statement in runSparseLookahead:
//   - Cases 1/2 player wins: buildDecisiveLine(bestTally, playedTally, 'player', rootBoard)
//   - Case 3 opponent punishes: buildDecisiveLine(oppTally, null, 'opponent', rootBoard)
function buildDecisiveLine(primaryTally, secondaryTally, owner, rootBoard) {
  const primaryWay   = pickEarliestWay(primaryTally);
  const secondaryWay = secondaryTally ? pickEarliestWay(secondaryTally) : null;
  if (!primaryWay && !secondaryWay) return undefined; // absent → pruned

  const fastWay  = (primaryWay && (!secondaryWay || primaryWay.ply <= secondaryWay.ply))
                   ? primaryWay : secondaryWay;
  const slowWay  = fastWay === primaryWay ? secondaryWay : primaryWay;
  const fastSide = fastWay === primaryWay ? 'best' : 'played'; // relative to Cases 1/2

  const completingCell = findGravityTopEmpty(fastWay.cells, rootBoard);
  return {
    owner,
    cells:                   fastWay.cells,
    completingCell,
    winningLinesThroughCell: countWindowsThrough(completingCell, rootBoard),
    fastSide,
    fastSideRealizedOnPly:  fastWay.ply,
    slowSideRealizedOnPly:  slowWay?.ply ?? null,
  };
}
```

**Owner field semantics**:
- Cases 1/2 (player wins best or played line): `owner: 'player'`, tallies from `bestTally` / `playedTally`.
- Case 3 (opponent punishes): `owner: 'opponent'`, tally from `oppTally` (opponent's perspective,
  separate scope — never co-exists with bestTally/playedTally in the same call).

**Absence rule**: if `buildDecisiveLine` returns `undefined`, `decisiveLine` is absent (pruned)
and `edgeType` must be `'positional'`.

**Absence rule**: if no `immediate_threat` way is found in the relevant tallies, `decisiveLine`
is absent from the return object (not `null`-in-object — it is simply not set, so `pruneEmpty`
removes it). `edgeType` must then be `'positional'`.

### 1.3 `reachability` (Story B — new field)

```js
reachability: {
  best:   { floor: 'win' | 'draw' | 'loss', ceiling: 'win' | 'draw' | 'loss' },
  played: { floor: 'win' | 'draw' | 'loss', ceiling: 'win' | 'draw' | 'loss' },
} | absent  // absent (pruned) when neither side's floor is "loss"
```

- `floor` = `toOutcome(optScore)` for the best side; `toOutcome(blunderScore)` for the played side.
  This is the same value as `outcomeTiming.*.outcome` — exposed here for semantic clarity.
- `ceiling` = best outcome reachable when the opponent errs, determined as follows:
  - **Non-losing floor side** (floor = 'win' or 'draw'): `ceiling = floor` — no search needed.
    A mistake-mode search cannot return a result better than a win, so this is provably equivalent.
  - **Losing floor side** (floor = 'loss'): run a **real mistake-mode search** on the relevant
    root. Pass `ceilingRef = { value: -Infinity }` into `searchOpportunities`; at each
    player-to-move node after `solver.query`, update `ceilingRef.value` with the max score seen.
    Map `ceilingRef.value` → outcome using `toOutcome`. Specific cases:
    - **Case 3**: use `ceilingRef` on the existing mistake-mode searches (no new pass needed).
    - **Cases 1/2 losing-played branch** (played floor = 'loss', played root was in OPTIMAL mode):
      add a **new explicit mistake-mode search pass** on the played root. The best root (floor ≠
      loss) does NOT need a new search — its ceiling = floor. Accept extra solver calls for the
      played-root pass (correctness-over-speed premise).
  - **Ceiling invariant**: ceiling ≥ floor at all times. The -Infinity→'loss' default is
    prohibited because it can produce ceiling < floor (e.g., floor='win' with ceiling='loss') —
    a contradiction and A4 fabrication source. Only emit ceiling from a real search or the
    ceiling = floor rule above.
- **Ceiling semantics**: ceiling = whether a usable opponent-mistake line exists within the search.
  ceiling = 'win' or 'draw' on a losing-floor side ⇒ a punishable opponent mistake was found
  within the search (not "provably" achievable — the search is bounded). ceiling = 'loss' on a
  losing-floor side ⇒ no winning line found within the search — but this does NOT mean "provably
  lost"; an opponent mistake beyond the search horizon may still exist. NEVER phrase ceiling = 'loss'
  as "lost cause" or "you cannot win" or "provably lost."
- **Emission gate**: only emitted when `floor` is `'loss'` for at least one side. When both sides
  win or draw, this field is absent. Both sides are ALWAYS present in the shape when emitted —
  even the non-losing side carries floor + ceiling (ceiling = floor for non-losing side).

**Joint reading with outcomeTiming**: `reachability` and `outcomeTiming` MUST be read together.
A floor = 'loss' side with a LARGER `outcomeTiming.pliesToEnd` = "you lose slower = more chances
for the opponent to err before the decisive outcome" — this is the primary reason why a
losing-floor move may still be worth playing. A smaller pliesToEnd = faster loss = fewer
opportunities. This joint reading is core to the epic's purpose and must be stated in the glossary.

### 1.4 `edgeType` (Story B — new field)

```js
edgeType: 'tactical' | 'positional' | 'marginal'
```

**Coarse branch (iteration 1 — ships now)** — ordered if/else, TOTAL (no undefined path):
```
if outcome(best) ≠ outcome(played):
    edgeType = "tactical"        // outcomes diverge between lines
else if decisiveLine is absent:
    edgeType = "positional"      // no decisive line found within horizon on either side
else:
    edgeType = "marginal"        // catch-all: same outcome, regardless of whether decisive line
                                 // found on one or both sides
```

This ordering is exhaustive — every position maps to exactly one value. The old "both sides" qualifier
on `marginal` is dropped; `marginal` is now the final catch-all covering same-outcome positions where
a decisive line exists on at least one side (single-line case and both-sides case are both `marginal`).

**Fine-grained branch** (K/D thresholds from R5): DEFERRED to follow-up iteration after Story A
lands and frozen vectors are regenerated. K and D must be empirically derived from actual
`pliesToEnd` values — they cannot be set before those values exist.

**Pruning safety**: `edgeType` is a non-empty string — it survives `pruneEmpty`. It is always set
on every one of the four return paths of `runSparseLookahead` (even if no decisive line was found).
A unit test must assert its presence on all four exit paths.

### 1.5 `categoryExamples` extended shape (Story B — shape change)

```js
categoryExamples: [
  {
    tag:           string,          // pattern category (from §4 vocabulary)
    bestNovel:     [{ cells: string[], realizedOnPly: number }],  // present on best, absent on played
    playedNovel:   [{ cells: string[], realizedOnPly: number }],  // present on played, absent on best
    novelInstances: number,         // total distinct novel cell-sets across both directions
    owner:         'player',
    severity?:     'immediate' | 'major' | 'minor',
  },
  ...
]
```

- A category appears only when `bestNovel` OR `playedNovel` is non-empty (true cell-set ties are
  dropped entirely).
- `bestNovel` replaces the old `ways` field. `playedNovel` is new (from the swapped second call).
- When a direction has no novel cell-sets, that key is omitted (not `[]`) so `pruneEmpty` handles
  it correctly. The caller always emits both keys and lets `toFeatureVector`'s `pruneEmpty` strip
  empty arrays.

**Breaking change from old `categoryExamples` shape** (old: `{ tag, ways, novelInstances }`):
The old `ways` field is removed; `bestNovel` is its replacement. Any consumer reading `ways` from
the feature vector must be updated. The feature-vector frozen set reader (`explain_from_vector.mjs`)
is a user-triggered step — not part of this epic.

### 1.6 `ceilingRef` dep (Story B — new optional dep on `searchOpportunities`)

```js
// Passed in deps; initialized before each mistake-mode search call:
const ceilingRef = { value: -Infinity };
// Inside searchOpportunities, at each player-to-move node after solver.query:
if (deps.ceilingRef) {
  for (const c of legal) {
    if (scores[c] > deps.ceilingRef.value) deps.ceilingRef.value = scores[c];
  }
}
```

**Usage by path**:
- **Case 3**: pass `ceilingRef` to the existing mistake-mode best/played searches — tracks ceiling
  within those searches at no extra solver cost.
- **Cases 1/2 losing-played branch** (played floor = 'loss'): a **new explicit mistake-mode search
  pass** is added on the played root. `ceilingRef` is passed to this new search. Accept extra
  solver calls (correctness over speed).
- **Cases 1/2 best side** (best floor ≠ 'loss'): `ceilingRef` is NOT used — best.ceiling = best.floor
  (no search needed; see §1.3 ceiling rule for non-losing floor sides).
- **Optimal-mode searches** (Cases 1/2 best root in optimal mode): `ceilingRef` is NOT passed —
  ceiling tracking is undefined for optimal-opponent play.

**Ceiling invariant**: After any mistake-mode search, `ceilingRef.value` represents the highest
player score reached at any player-to-move node. This score, mapped via `toOutcome`, gives the
ceiling. Ceiling ≥ floor is guaranteed when the search is sound (if the player's floor is 'loss',
any player-perspective node score ≥ the floor score by definition).

## 2. `toFeatureVector` projection (explainContext.js)

### 2.1 `lookahead` block — new projected fields

All projected inside the existing `lookahead: la ? { ... } : null` block.

```js
lookahead: la ? {
  case:               la.case,
  bestOutcome:        la.bestOutcome ?? null,
  postBlunderOutcome: la.postBlunderOutcome ?? null,

  // NEW (Story A):
  outcomeTiming: la.outcomeTiming ?? undefined,  // pruned when absent

  // NEW (Story A): present only when a completing window was found within horizon
  decisiveLine: la.decisiveLine ?? undefined,   // pruned when absent

  // NEW (Story B): present only when at least one side's floor is "loss"
  reachability: la.reachability ?? undefined,   // pruned when absent

  // NEW (Story B): always present when lookahead ran
  edgeType: la.edgeType,

  // CHANGED (Story B): shape change from { tag, ways, novelInstances } to symmetric shape
  categoryExamples: (la.categoryExamples ?? []).map((e) => ({
    tag:           e.tag,
    owner:         'player',
    severity:      severityTag({ ...e, owner: 'player' }).severity,  // severityTag (explainContext.js:109, used at :265-266)
    bestNovel:     e.bestNovel?.length   ? e.bestNovel   : undefined,  // pruned if empty
    playedNovel:   e.playedNovel?.length ? e.playedNovel : undefined,  // pruned if empty
    novelInstances: e.novelInstances,
  })),

  // oppCategoryExamples: unchanged shape (best-novel only, from opponent perspective)
  oppCategoryExamples: (la.oppCategoryExamples ?? []).map((e) => severityTag({ ...e, owner: 'opponent' })),

  // perCategory: REMOVED from feature vector (superseded by symmetric categoryExamples).
  // The tallyComparison data is still available on rawLookahead for prompt_data / debugging,
  // but is no longer projected into the feature vector.
  // NOTE: The production lookaheadSection does NOT read perCategory from the feature vector
  // (it reads la.tag / la.aliasMap directly), so this removal is safe.
} : null,
```

**`perCategory` removal**: The old count-based `perCategory` table (`{ tag, bestInstances,
playedInstances }`) is removed from the feature vector projection. Its role is fully superseded
by the symmetric `categoryExamples`. The `tallyComparison` data remains on `rawLookahead` for
`prompt_data` debugging but is NOT projected into `featureVector`.

### 2.2 `threatStats` — new total fields (Story C)

Inside `compactThreats` (or a thin wrapper called from the `...(() => { ... })()` IIFE in
`toFeatureVector`):

```js
// Added to each threatStats.<state> snapshot:
playerMajorTotal:   (snap.playerMajorParityAligned?.count ?? 0) + (snap.playerMajorNonParity?.count ?? 0),
opponentMajorTotal: (snap.opponentMajorParityAligned?.count ?? 0) + (snap.opponentMajorNonParity?.count ?? 0),
```

**Pruning behavior**: when the total is 0, `pruneEmpty` removes it (number 0 is falsey-deep per
`isZeroOrBlankDeep`). This is correct and intentional — absence of `playerMajorTotal` means "no
major threats" (FR-C03).

**Where**: the `compactThreats` function already returns a compact snapshot. The sum can be added
there or in the IIFE that calls it. Prefer adding it inside `compactThreats` for locality.

## 3. Glossary changes (docs/architecture/feature-vector-glossary.md)

### §2 (Top-level fields) — no change (playedCol already documented)

### §5.1 (`patterns*` maps) — Story C addition

Add after the existing three-snapshot description:

> **Snapshot provenance** — which board each map describes:
> - `patternsPreMove` — the board **before either move** (root position, `movestring` exactly).
> - `patternsBest` — the board **after the better move** lands (the board you would have
>   produced with `bestCol`).
> - `patternsPostBlunder` — the board **after the played move** lands (the board you actually
>   produced).
> - `patternsOpponent` — the **opponent's structures on the pre-move board** (the classifier run
>   from the opponent's perspective on `movestring`, before either move was made). This is NOT
>   the opponent's structures after the played move — it is a static snapshot of the pre-move
>   threat landscape from the opponent's side.

### §5.2 (`threatStats`) — Story C addition

Add after the bucket table:

> **Major-threat totals** — each snapshot also carries `playerMajorTotal` (the sum of
> `playerMajorParityAligned.count` and `playerMajorNonParity.count`) and `opponentMajorTotal`
> (the sum of the two opponent major buckets). When either total is zero, the field is absent
> (pruned — absence = "no major threats"). **"Zero parity-aligned majors ≠ zero majors."** A
> player with `playerMajorParityAligned` absent but `playerMajorNonParity` present still has a
> major threat — the `playerMajorTotal` (and the `playerMajorNonParity` bucket) make this
> explicit.

### §5.3 (`lookahead`) — Stories A and B additions

Replace the existing `lookahead` block description with the following extended version (keeping
the existing fields and adding new ones):

**New fields to document** (in §5.3):

`outcomeTiming`:
> Per-side outcome and distance-to-decisive-event. Used comparatively to say "you win/lose faster
> vs. slower." `pliesToEnd` is the number of moves (plies) until the decisive outcome appears
> under optimal play, derived from the solver score magnitude. It is **NOT** the same as
> `realizedOnPly` (which measures depth along the mistake branch, from the player-to-move
> position) and **NOT** raw solver-score magnitude exposed bare. `pliesToEnd` is null for draws
> or when the solver cannot provide a magnitude.
>
> **Presence rule**: `outcomeTiming` is present whenever `lookahead` ran — it is NOT conditional
> on `reachability` or `decisiveLine`. A draw or solver error yields `pliesToEnd: null` but the
> `outcome` field still carries information; the field is never pruned when a lookahead result
> exists. Legitimately absent only when `lookahead` itself is null (no search ran).
>
> **Read jointly with `reachability`**: on a losing-floor side, a larger `pliesToEnd` means slower
> loss — more time for the opponent to err. This joint signal is the primary reason a losing move
> may still be worth playing over a faster-losing alternative.

`decisiveLine`:
> The completing 4-window found within the search horizon. Absent (pruned) when no concrete
> winning line was found within the search depth — in that case, `edgeType` is `"positional"`.
> `winningLinesThroughCell` = 1 means a single-line win; > 1 means a genuine multi-line fork
> (the "double threat" distinction). `fastSide` is the move line (`"best"` or `"played"`) on
> which this completing window appears soonest. `owner` says whether it is your win or the
> opponent's.

`reachability`:
> Floor (outcome under perfect opponent play) and ceiling (best outcome reachable **within the
> search** if the opponent errs). The ceiling is **never** "provably" achievable — it is the best
> result found within the bounded search depth. `ceiling = 'win'` or `'draw'` on a losing-floor
> side means a punishable opponent-mistake line **was found within the search**; `ceiling = 'loss'`
> means no such line was found within the search — **never** say "lost cause," "you cannot win," or
> "provably lost." Absent when neither side's floor is `"loss"`. For non-losing floor sides, ceiling
> equals floor (no new search needed; provably equivalent). Both sides are always present in the
> shape when the field is emitted.
>
> **Read jointly with `outcomeTiming`**: a losing-floor side with a larger `pliesToEnd` loses
> slower — more chances for the opponent to err. This joint signal is the primary reason such a
> move may still be worth playing.

`edgeType`:
> The nature of the positional difference. Derived via ordered if/else (total — no undefined path):
> `"tactical"` = the outcomes diverge between the two lines (one wins, the other loses or draws).
> `"positional"` = no decisive line found within the horizon on either side (`decisiveLine` absent).
> `"marginal"` = catch-all: same outcome on both lines (decisive line may be present on one or both
> sides, or on neither when both sides draw). Always present when lookahead ran (a truthy enum —
> never absent).

`categoryExamples` (updated):
> Each entry now carries **both** `bestNovel` (cell-sets present on the better line, absent on
> the played line) and `playedNovel` (cell-sets present on the played line, absent on the better
> line), each with per-cell `realizedOnPly` timing. A category appears only when its cell-sets
> differ between the two lines. `bestNovel` or `playedNovel` may each be absent when only one
> direction has novel cells for that category. A high `realizedOnPly` in either direction means
> the structure is a **projected future structure**, not a threat on the current board.

**Timing discipline statement** (to add at top of §5.3):

> **Present-vs-projected discipline.** The `lookahead` block describes structures found during
> a forward search, not structures on the current board. Every `realizedOnPly` value (whether
> in `categoryExamples`, `decisiveLine`, or `oppCategoryExamples`) tells you how many plies
> into the future the structure was found. A `realizedOnPly` of 1 means it appears on the
> immediate resulting board; larger values mean deeper in the search. **Never describe a
> structure with `realizedOnPly > 1` as already present on the board.**
>
> **Three distinct timing concepts — do not conflate:**
> - `realizedOnPly` — depth (in plies) at which a structure appears in the forward search, from
>   the pre-move position. Measures "how deep in the mistake branch."
> - `outcomeTiming.pliesToEnd` — distance-to-decisive-event: how many moves until the decisive
>   outcome appears under optimal play, derived from the solver score. Used comparatively between
>   the two lines. Measures "how far until the game is decided."
> - "mate distance" — the number of moves until checkmate / forced win, a concept from classical
>   chess engines. The two fields above are Connect Four equivalents but with different semantics;
>   neither is a direct "mate distance."

## 4. Characterization test fixture (Story B precondition)

The characterization test must snapshot `allowedSet` and `aliasMap` for a fixed subset of
eval positions before any edit to `collectNovelOpportunities` or `compareOpportunities`.

**Fixture positions** (use a subset of the 18 frozen cases that cover all lookahead cases):
- Case 1 (better holds, played loses): eval-0 or eval-8
- Case 2 (both hold, better stronger): eval-12 or eval-29
- Case 3 (losing either way): eval-42 or eval-56

**Snapshot format**:
```js
// Snapshot assertion (pseudo-code):
assert.deepStrictEqual(
  { allowedSet: result.allowedSet, aliasMap: result.aliasMap },
  SNAPSHOTS[positionId]
);
```

The snapshots are committed to the test file as inline constants. Any change to
`collectNovelOpportunities` / `compareOpportunities` that alters these outputs is a production
regression and must be investigated before merging.

## 5. Unit test plan

### Story A tests (`sparseLookahead.test.js` — new file)

| Test | Input | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| A-T1 | Win-in-5 position (optScore=+5) | `outcomeTiming.best.pliesToEnd = 5`, `outcome = 'win'` |
| A-T2 | Draw position (optScore=0) | `outcomeTiming.best.pliesToEnd = null`, `outcome = 'draw'` |
| A-T3 | Solver error (score undefined) | `outcomeTiming.best.pliesToEnd = null`, `outcome = null` |
| A-T4 | Position with `immediate_threat` in tally | `decisiveLine.cells` = 4-window, `winningLinesThroughCell` ≥ 1 |
| A-T5 | Single-line immediate win | `decisiveLine.winningLinesThroughCell = 1` |
| A-T6 | Fork (two winning lines through completing cell) | `decisiveLine.winningLinesThroughCell = 2` |
| A-T7 | Horizon-exceeded position (no `immediate_threat` in tally) | `decisiveLine` absent, `edgeType = 'positional'` |
| A-T8 | Best wins faster than played | `decisiveLine.fastSide = 'best'`, `fastSideRealizedOnPly < slowSideRealizedOnPly` |
| A-T9 | All four return paths of `runSparseLookahead` | `edgeType` present (truthy string) and `outcomeTiming` present on every exit — no silent drop |
| A-T9b | Forced-outcome position (win or loss on both sides) | `outcomeTiming` present with non-null `pliesToEnd` for the decisive sides |
| A-T9c | Draw/no-forced-outcome fixture (score=0 both sides) | `outcomeTiming` present with `pliesToEnd: null`; field not absent; `edgeType` is `'positional'` or `'marginal'` |

### Story B tests (`sparseLookahead.test.js` and `explainContext.test.js`)

| Test | Input | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| B-T1 | True cell-set tie (same cells on both lines for a tag) | That tag absent from `categoryExamples` |
| B-T2 | Category with different cells on each line | `bestNovel` non-empty, `playedNovel` non-empty, each with `realizedOnPly` |
| B-T3 | Category present only on best line | `bestNovel` non-empty, `playedNovel` absent |
| B-T4 | Category present only on played line | `bestNovel` absent, `playedNovel` non-empty |
| B-T5 | Losing-either-way position | `reachability.best.floor = 'loss'`, `reachability.played.floor = 'loss'` |
| B-T6 | Best-holds, played-loses (Case-1) | `reachability` emitted (played floor = 'loss'); `reachability.best.ceiling = reachability.best.floor` (best floor ≠ 'loss' → no search needed); `reachability.played.ceiling` derived from real mistake-mode search |
| B-T7 | Outcome diverges between lines | `edgeType = 'tactical'` |
| B-T8 | No line within horizon on either side | `edgeType = 'positional'` |
| B-T9 | Same outcome + decisive line found on ONE side only (single-line fixture) | `edgeType = 'marginal'` (catch-all — not "both sides" required) |
| B-T9b | Same outcome, decisive line found on BOTH sides | `edgeType = 'marginal'` (same catch-all path) |
| B-T10 | Characterization snapshot regression | `allowedSet`/`aliasMap` byte-identical for 3 fixture positions |
| B-T11 | Case 3 position (opponent punishes) | `decisiveLine.owner = 'opponent'`, `decisiveLine.cells` from `oppTally`, not bestTally/playedTally |
| B-T12 | Cases 1/2 losing-played branch (Case-1 record) | `reachability` emitted; `played.ceiling ≥ played.floor` from real mistake-mode search (not -Infinity default); `best.ceiling = best.floor` since best floor is not 'loss' |
